newsitem.title: USA: Snyder Oil 1997 capital budget of $112 mln.
newsitem.headline: Snyder Oil 1997 capital budget of $112 mln.

text.p: Snyder Oil Corp said Monday that its board has approved a capital budget of $112 million for 1997, excluding acquisitions. The figure is a 120 percent increase from the $51 million invested in 1996, the company said.
"We believe that this budget puts us on track to increase company-wide production by roughly one-third over a two-year period, based solely on internal growth," the company said in a release.

It also said it is trying to achieve its goal of boosting daily production volumes by two-thirds -- from last year's average of 36,040 BOE per day -- before the end of 1998. Such a goal would result in 60,000 BOE per day by the end of next year and mean "a dramatic increase in cash flow per share," it said.
Snyder said the 1997 capital budget includes $85 million for development programs, $19 million for expanding exploratory activity and $8 million for GPM and other activities.
It said it expects to drill 124 wells domestically in 1997, up from 85 wells in 1996.
